messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: dedicated capacity fit & $/1M token targets - Nimbus

Thanks again for the demo time earlier — quick recap and next steps from our side. High-level notes from the call: 

- Primary ask: dedicated capacity to support production chat/assistant workload (transformer LM) with predictable latency and cost.
- Steady-state tokens: you mentioned ~3–4M tokens/day (roughly 90–120M/month).
- Peak day bursts: up to ~18–20M tokens/day during product events.
- Latency target: p95 < 350ms for ~256-token responses; spike tolerance higher but prefer graceful degradation.
- Preferred hardware: you said H100 preferred for throughput; open to A100 if it materially reduces unit cost.
- Budget/Unit economics ask: target $/1M tokens in the ballpark of $150–$350 (you mentioned wanting to understand effective $/1M after reserved pricing).

What we (Redwood) will deliver as next steps:
- Ben will size two initial reserved options (low-commit and performance-first) with monthly pricing and the implied effective $/1M tokens.
- I'll include contract length options (1yr / 3yr) and uplift for 24/7 enterprise support and SLA.
- We'll attach a preliminary quote + high-level perf numbers and a short checklist of runtime assumptions (sequence length distribution, concurrency, prefix caching).

Action requests for you:
- Confirm steady-state tokens/day (single number or tighter range).
- Share a small sample of request payloads (batch of 50-100 typical prompts) and peak QPS expectations. A CSV is fine.
- Any procurement lead or PO cadence we should know about for Reserved capacity?

I've attached a small template (nimbus_payload_samples.csv) — if you can drop that back to me by EOD Tue we'll try to get a draft quote to you within 48 hours.

Thanks — Lauren

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers inline: 

- Steady-state: planning for ~3.5M tokens/day (we forecast ~105M/month once live).
- Peak: during launches we see spikes up to ~18M tokens/day; want headroom for ~20M to be safe.
- Latency: p95 <350ms for 256 tokens is our internal SLA target. If there are tradeoffs between latency and cost, we need explicit options and best-effort fallbacks.
- Hardware preference: H100 would be our first choice (we run other heavy inference there), but if A100 yields substantially better economics we'd consider it.
- Target unit economics: we're evaluating effective $/1M tokens in the $150–$300 range, depending on SLA/commitment term.

Procurement: procurement lead is Mike O'Leary (cc'd). For big purchases, we generally run 1yr commitments but will consider 3yr for better unit pricing.

I attached a sample of typical prompts and average response lengths — hope that helps with sizing.

Erin — thanks for the numbers, that's very helpful. Based on the sample payloads and the token profile you sent, I've sketched two reserved options to match your steady-state + peak requirements. Notes below are preliminary — final quote coming as a PDF.

Option A — Performance-focused (H100, lower latency)
- Config: 2 x H100 (shared KV cache per cluster), dedicated networking, 24/7 enterprise support.
- Estimated throughput: handles ~20M tokens/day with p95 ~300ms at 256-token responses, headroom for short bursting.
- Monthly reserved cost: $30,000
- Effective unit: with 105M monthly tokens -> ~$285 per 1M tokens (without overage).
- Pros: meets latency SLO with margin; fewer nodes so simpler rollout.
- Cons: higher unit price vs higher-commit A100 options.

Option B — Capacity/Cost-optimized (A100-80GB band)
- Config: 4 x A100-80GB (lower per-GPU price, more nodes), standard enterprise support.
- Estimated throughput: handles ~22–25M tokens/day with p95 ~360ms at 256-token responses.
- Monthly reserved cost: $28,000
- Effective unit: with 105M monthly tokens -> ~$267 per 1M tokens.
- Pros: better unit economics; more redundancy.
- Cons: slightly higher p95; may need tuning for peak behavior.

Other considerations / assumptions
- We assume average response length ~220 tokens, request+response ~300 tokens. If your real distribution skews longer we'll need an extra GPU for headroom.
- Caching: prefix and KV caching is applied by default; if you use long-running chat sessions with large KV cache requirements we may need more memory (affects A100 vs H100 choice).
- Contract term: 12-month vs 36-month will change unit pricing materially; I'll include both in the quote.

Attached: redwood-dedicated-pricing-v2.pdf (prelim pricing matrix + perf notes).

Next steps I propose:
1) Lauren to share 1-yr and 3-yr priced options and a short T&Cs checklist.
2) Mike to confirm procurement timeline so we can align PO/discounting.
3) If you want, we can set a short perf validation window (2–3 days) on a small test cluster to validate p95 numbers against a representative load.

Happy to jump on a 20–30 minute call to walk through the numbers — pinged Lauren for scheduling.

— Ben
Ben Carter

Thanks Ben — that framing is exactly what we needed. We're inclined toward Option A (2x H100) because meeting p95 is a priority during interactive demos; the higher unit cost is acceptable if the SLA holds.

Requests before we proceed with PO:
- Please include both 12-month and 36-month pricing lines (showing per-1M token effective cost).
- Add SOC 2 type II evidence and standard security addenda (we'll run that through our security review).
- Include options for a 3-day perf validation window (instrumented) and the expected test harness steps.

Procurement timeline: we can get a PO issued within 2–3 weeks once paperwork + SOC2 is provided. Mike will own that.

If you can turn the formal quote and evidence by EOD Wed we'll aim to review and come back with comments by the following Monday.

Erin
